heroNote: MIT code · CC BY-NC-SA fiction · public reading without an account.
premiseBody: CIRCA — the Commission for Incident Review and Corrective Action — is not a government agency. It is a continuity: a bureaucracy that has attached itself to whatever power structure was available for long enough that nobody remembers its first name. It reviews incidents that should not have happened, and files reports about them. It does not correct reality. It files paperwork on it.
premiseBodyTwo: The archive is a story and an interface at the same time. Every record is authored as Markdown, and every record is also a plate of codes, clearance levels, redactions, and citations that point at other records. The worldbuilding lives in that machinery: a document that behaves like paperwork is easier to believe than one that behaves like prose.
quote: CIRCA does not decide what is true. It decides what is on file.
quoteAttribution: Central principle of the Commission — in fiction, and in the code.
specimenText: A free-standing door in a pasture in Gangwon Province. No walls. No frame beyond the door itself. It has been there for at least sixty years, possibly longer. It does not move. It does not open on its own. It is, by every available measure, a door.
specimenNote: One of the authored records. Sample content, not canon.
editionsTitle: The same records, read two ways.
editionsLede: Everything on this site is one of two things: something you read, or something you operate. Both editions render the same corpus from the same source.
readingBody: A typographic reading edition, rendered on the server. Every record has its own page, its own citation trail, and its own copy of the Markdown it was built from. Public reading is complete without JavaScript.
workstationBody: A workstation that behaves like the operating system of an institution that never existed: a record viewer, a correspondence client, a filing desk. Its records are illustrative fixtures; notes, replies, and editor drafts stay in the current tab.
editionsNote: Both archive editions use illustrative records. Personal accounts are connected to the authentication service; notes and drafts remain in the browser.
builtLede: The fiction is the easy part. Most of the work is the machinery that keeps one record legible in both editions.
factRecordsDetail: Markdown with frontmatter, authored by hand and supplied as archive fixtures. Accounts are stored separately by the authentication service.
factPipelineDetail: remark, with plugins that withhold redacted text, resolve figure directives, and anchor headings. One parsed document feeds both editions.
factPagesDetail: Next.js App Router. The portal and archive resolve personal access on each request; record content remains fixture-backed in both languages.
factInterfaceDetail: React server components and CSS Modules. No component library on the reading edition, and no client JavaScript there.
factLanguageDetail: English and Korean, routed at /en and /ko. One catalog per language; no sentence is written inside a component.
factTestsDetail: Vitest for the interface and its rules. The pre-commit hook runs lint, typecheck, and the suite before anything lands.
factLicenceDetail: MIT for the code, Creative Commons for the fiction. Both are set out further down this page.
builtNote: Sign-up, sign-in, and personal access are connected to the .NET backend and its account database. Archive records, notes, and workstation drafts remain illustrative or local. No visit tracking is used.
contributeTitle: The archive grows by being written.
contributeLede: CIRCA Archive is pre-production and open. Records, continuities, organizations, interface work, and corrections are all welcome — and no contributor is asked to sign anything.
stepGuideBody: Scope, conventions, and an honest account of what is finished. A proposed continuity belongs in an issue before it becomes a pull request.
stepChangeBody: One coherent change per branch, with the lockfile committed and generated folders left alone.
stepChecksBody: The pre-commit hook verifies staged READMEs, repository tooling, lint, types, and the unit suite.
contributeNote: Correspondence about the fiction, the code, or a broken record belongs in the repository's issues.
contributorsLede: CIRCA Archive is maintained in the open. Anyone who writes a record, corrects a page, or files a useful report is credited here. Contributing through the repository does not require a site account.
contributorsMaintainerWork: Records, interface, and the archive's estate.
contributorsNote: Records carry their author's name beside the seal. Everything else is credited here and in the commit history.
supportBody: CIRCA Archive is a personal design and worldbuilding project. No company sits behind it, and nothing here is for sale. Support pays for the domain, the hosting, and the hours it takes to read pull requests and keep the archive's records consistent with one another.
supportSponsorBody: Recurring or one-time, through GitHub Sponsors. No tier, no badge, no obligation.
supportPromise: Nothing on this site is paywalled. The records, the source, and the licence stay open either way.
faqLede: The questions that arrive most often, with the answers the project actually gives.
faqRealA: No. The Commission, its offices, its correspondents, and every incident on file are invented. The site names no real agency and describes no real event. The interface, the records, and the argument for them are real work.
faqWriteA: That is the point of the archive. Read the contribution guide, open an issue with the continuity you have in mind, then file the record as Markdown. Records are reviewed for consistency with what is already on file, not for canon.
faqNotesA: Notes, drafts, and replies stay in the browser tab and are lost when it closes; they are not sent to the archive service. Account registration and sign-in use the authentication backend and store account and session data separately.
faqReuseQ: Can I reuse the records or the code?
faqReuseA: The code is MIT. The records, the fiction, and the artwork are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: share and adapt them with attribution, non-commercially, under the same licence. The seal belongs to the fiction.
faqLanguageA: English is the language the archive's paperwork was written in; Korean is there because the Commission keeps correspondents in the Republic of Korea. Neither is a translation of the other: every page, record, and label exists in both.
faqRoadmapQ: What is finished, and what is not?
faqRoadmapA: The reading edition and workstation preview are available. Account registration, sign-in, and personal access are connected to the .NET backend. Archive domain services, saved annotations, and publishing remain in development.
contactLede: Three doors. None of them needs an account, and all of them reach the same maintainer.
channelBugBody: A page that will not render, a record that will not open, a link that dead-ends, a table that will not align.
channelFeatureBody: A missing affordance, a new continuity, a better way to read the citation web.
channelContactBody: Press, permissions, a record that carries your name, or anything the two forms above do not cover.
contactNote: Reports and proposals are read in the open, in the repository. Nothing sent from this page is stored by the site itself.
licenceTitle: MIT for the code. CC for the fiction.
licenceLede: The repository holds two different kinds of thing, so it carries two licences. The terms are short, because there is almost nothing here to accept.
licenceCodeBody: The application, the render pipeline, and the stylesheets. Use it, change it, ship it — keep the copyright notice.
licenceContentBody: The records, the fiction, and the artwork. Share and adapt them with attribution, non-commercially, under the same licence.
licenceFiction: Nothing here is real. No agency, office, correspondent, or incident described on this site exists.
licenceAccounts: Accounts hold your username and email and use essential session cookies. There are no payments or correspondence delivery.
licenceCookie: One cookie remembers your language. No analytics, no third-party scripts, no profile.
licenceWarranty: Provided as is. Nothing on this site is advice, an offer, or a service.
licenceFootnote: Corrections, takedowns, and reports go to the repository's issues.
